arxiv-2003-04827.creator: David I. Spivak, David Jaz Myers
arxiv-2003-04827.description: Abstract One can think of power series or polynomials in one variable, such as P ⁡ ( 𝓎 ) = 2 ​ 𝓎 3 + 𝓎 + 5 P(\mathcal{y})=2\mathcal{y}^{3}+\mathcal{y}+5 , as functors from the category 𝖲𝖾𝗍 \mathsf{Set} of sets to itself; these are known as polynomial functors.

arxiv-2107-03108.title: Groups whose Chermak-Delgado lattice is a subgroup lattice of an elementary abelian p p -group Thanks: This work was supported by NSFC (No. 11971280 &11771258)
arxiv-2107-03108.creator: Lijian An
arxiv-2107-03108.description: Abstract The Chermak-Delgado lattice of a finite group G G is a self-dual sublattice of the subgroup lattice of G G . In this paper, we focus on finite groups whose Chermak-Delgado lattice is a subgroup lattice of an elementary abelian p p -group. We prove that such groups are nilpotent of class 2 2 .

arxiv-2112-04183.title: Twin-Distance-Hereditary Digraphs
arxiv-2112-04183.creator: Dominique Komander, Carolin Rehs
arxiv-2112-04183.description: Abstract We investigate structural and algorithmic advantages of a directed version of the well-researched class of distance-hereditary graphs. Since the previously defined distance-hereditary digraphs do not permit a recursive structure, we define directed twin-distance-hereditary graphs, which can be constructed by several twin and pendant vertex operations analogously to undirected distance-hereditary graphs and which still preserves the distance hereditary property.

arxiv-2205-15546.title: Identifying and Characterizing Silently-Evolved Methods in the Android API
arxiv-2205-15546.creator: Pei Liu 1 , Li Li 1 α , Yichun Yan 2 , Mattia Fazzini 2 , John Grundy 1
arxiv-2205-15546.description: Abstract With over 500,000 commits and more than 700 contributors, the Android platform is undoubtedly one of the largest industrial-scale software projects. This project provides the Android API, and developers heavily rely on this API to develop their Android apps.

arxiv-2208-12821.title: Multiple locations of near-infrared coronal lines in NGC 5548 2022 Multiple locations of near-infrared coronal lines in NGC 5548 – 16
arxiv-2208-12821.creator: Daniel Kynoch, Hermine Landt, Maryam Dehghanian, Martin J. Ward and Gary J. Ferland
arxiv-2208-12821.description: Abstract We present the first intensive study of the variability of the near-infrared coronal lines in an active galactic nucleus (AGN). We use data from a one-year long spectroscopic monitoring campaign with roughly weekly cadence on NGC 5548 to study the variability in both emission line fluxes and profile shapes.

arxiv-2305-03157.title: Good Will Hunting’s Problem: Counting Homeomorphically Irreducible Trees
arxiv-2305-03157.creator: Ira M. Gessel ∗
arxiv-2305-03157.description: Abstract . In the film Good Will Hunting , the main character, a janitor at MIT named Will Hunting, attacks the problem of drawing all the homeomorphically irreducible trees with 10 vertices. Although the film suggests that this is a difficult problem, it is in fact quite easy.

arxiv-2311-12516.creator: Tiziana Di Salvo, Alessandro Papitto, Alessio Marino, Rosario Iaria and Luciano Burderi

arxiv-2405-10059.title: Discussing Risks and Benefits in the Future of Hybrid Rehabilitation and Fitness in Mixed Reality
arxiv-2405-10059.creator: Jana Funke Enrico Rukzio
arxiv-2405-10059.description: Abstract In a world where in-person context transitions more into remote and hybrid concepts, we should consider new concepts of interaction in health and rehabilitation and what advantages and disadvantages they bring. One of the rising topics is mixed reality, where we can use the advantages of immersive 3D, 360-degree environments.

arxiv-2406-00361.title: Velocity decorrelation functions of high-energy cosmic rays propagating in magnetic fields
arxiv-2406-00361.creator: Olivier Deligny
arxiv-2406-00361.description: Abstract Diffusion tensor coefficients play a central role in describing cosmic-ray transport in various astrophysical environments permeated with magnetic fields, which are usually modeled as a fluctuating field on top of a mean field. In this article, a formal derivation of these coefficients is presented by means of the calculation of velocity decorrelation functions of particles.

arxiv-2410-14071.title: Appropriateness of the McNamara and Buland’s (2004) methodology for computing frequency-dependent seismic power
arxiv-2410-14071.creator: Sebin John, Michael E. West
arxiv-2410-14071.description: Abstract The methodology developed by McNamara and Buland (2004) for computing Power Spectral Densities (PSDs) has gained popularity due to its low computational cost and reduction of spectral variance. This methodology is widely used in seismic noise studies and station performance evaluations and is implemented in tools like ISPAQ, MUSTANG, and PQLX.

pmc-12372178.title: Beyond dietary therapy: addressing weight stigma awareness in medical students
pmc-12372178.creator: Giuseppe Annunziata, Giordano Bruno Zonzini, Evelyn Frias-Toral, Raynier Zambrano-Villacres, Alexander Bertuccioli, Davide Sisti, Ludovica Verde, Daniele Di Pauli, Annamaria Colao, Giovanna Muscogiuri, Daniel Simancas-Racines, Alessandro Gennaro, Luigi Barrea
pmc-12372178.description: BackgroundThe growing prevalence of obesity worldwide has drawn increased attention to the issue of weight stigma. Discriminatory attitudes related to body weight are evident across various settings, including those that should ideally offer support to individuals with obesity, such as schools and sports facilities. This research aimed to examine weight-related stigma among university students enrolled in healthcare-related academic programs.

pmc-13347742.title: Three novel Rothia species associated with Antarctic birds harbour novel biosynthetic gene clusters
pmc-13347742.creator: Vendula Koublová, Jana Musilova, Karel Sedlar, Peter Spacek, Jitka Vives, Eva Staňková, Ondrej Šedo, Stanislava Kralova, Ludek Sehnal, Ivo Sedláček, Pavel Švec
pmc-13347742.description: Antarctica's unique environment supports diverse avian populations, including penguins, skuas, and gulls. As climate-driven pressures on these populations intensify, their microbiota receives increased attention due to their relevance for host health. In this study, we investigated 11 bacterial isolates associated with Antarctic birds using a polyphasic taxonomic approach integrating genomic and phenotypic data.

pmc-13380501.title: Fluorometric toolkit for methanethiol quantification and methanethiol oxidase activity determination in biological systems
pmc-13380501.creator: Thilo M Philipp, Belen Schiffmann, Lucie K Tintrop, Jacqueline Findlay, Niklas Krafczyk, Hanna Schlemminger, Susana Ainsa-Zazurca, Vicente Ferreira, Pascal Fuchsmann, Patrice Nordmann, Lars-Oliver Klotz, Csaba Szabo, Tomas Majtan
pmc-13380501.description: Methanethiol (MeSH) is a pivotal volatile sulfur compound in plant, human, and environmental chemistry, but its study is hindered by analytical challenges. Here, we present an accessible fluorometric two-component assay toolkit for quantitative assessment of its content and enzymatic degradation by methanethiol oxidase (MTO).

pmc-13481051.description: focusing on pregnancy, childbirth, and reproductive health. The NPM program in India, initiated in 2019, is an 18-month government initiative to enhance maternal healthcare by creating a professional midwifery workforce.[2] This initiative addresses previous approaches where midwifery was merged with general nursing, leading to unclear roles and underutilized midwifery skills.

pmc-13486425.title: Translation and cultural adaptation of the health literacy questionnaire (HLQ) in Morocco
pmc-13486425.creator: Karima Boumendil, Younes Iderdar, Nadia Al Wachami, Maryem Arraji, Salwa Najmi, Melanie Hawkins, Richard Osborne, Mohamed Chahboune
pmc-13486425.description: BackgroundHealth literacy is an established determinant of health and a key tool in the development of public health interventions. It plays an important role in improving the health and equity of individuals and populations. The Health Literacy Questionnaire (HLQ) is a widely used multidimensional instrument designed to assess various domains of health literacy across diverse populations.
